source: VVOB Cambodia / MAFF Kampong Thom Provincial Department of Agriculture — IPM and Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for Rice, 9-point training presentation, presenter Mr. Tem Seng, Oct 5, 2010 (training slide deck; no elibrary URL visible)
text: Good seed selection is the first step of the nine-point rice good agricultural practices (ប.វ.ស) taught in this training. Farmers should use pure, clean seed (ពូជសុទ្ធ) that has been well sorted and shows high quality, rather than mixed or leftover seed. Two checks are recommended before sowing: (1) a small germination trial (ការបណ្តុះសាក) — soak a sample of the seed lot and check how many grains sprout before committing the full batch, and (2) selecting only filled, heavy grains for sowing by winnowing or floating off empty/light grains (ការជ្រើសរើសយកគ្រាប់ពេញទៅសាប), discarding grains that float or feel light, since these are less likely to germinate well or produce vigorous seedlings. This approach avoids wasting scarce good seed on the poorer fraction of a seed lot and gives more even seedling emergence in the nursery bed.
